demographics.trauma_type: Unexpected or traumatic death of a loved one

Maladaptive Strategies.value: I avoid eating or restrict food as a way of coping

Memory.value: When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event.
When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop
I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind.

Negative Appraisals.value: I have lost my faith in people, life, or a higher power
Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore
My life has been destroyed by the trauma

issues.explanation: For trauma type 'unexpected or traumatic death of a loved one', the body-focused appraisals 'I can no longer trust my own body' and 'I feel ashamed of what happened to my body' are hard to reconcile clinically unless the patient also directly experienced major bodily violation/injury, which is not reflected elsewhere in the profile.

The memory items imply vivid sensory reliving of the traumatic event ('hear things ... heard during the frightening event') and fragmented visual snapshots, which can occur in PTSD, but here they are not well matched to the selected appraisals: the profile centers on bodily shame/unreliability rather than grief/death-related meanings of the event.

'Avoid Work or Study: Going to work or study' is not impossible, but in this profile it appears weakly integrated: there are no trigger or threat items tying work contexts to the trauma, and the formulation does not include trigger/threat pathways. The coping profile otherwise concerns sleep delay and undereating, so work avoidance feels insufficiently anchored.

issues.item: Body Shame: I feel ashamed of what happened to my body
issues.explanation: For trauma involving the unexpected or traumatic death of a loved one, body-focused shame is clinically hard to reconcile unless there was also direct bodily violation, injury, or assault. The rest of the profile centers grief-related loss, meaning, and intrusive memory phenomena, so this item appears inconsistent with the trauma type and with the other selected items.

vignette: Makayla, a 46-year-old married woman of Oceania descent, had been working as a forensic analyst for over a decade when her life took an unbearable turn. Her younger brother, a free-spirited artist, died suddenly in a tragic accident while traveling abroad. Makayla was devastated by the loss, and the trauma of that event still reverberates through every aspect of her life. The memories of that day, especially the phone call she received with the news, are forever etched in her mind like snapshots – vivid moments frozen in time. Whenever these memories surface, Makayla feels overwhelmed by emotion, forced to stop whatever she's doing and retreat into herself. She sometimes hears the sound of her own screams or the eerie silence that followed, replaying them over and over in her head like a haunting echo. Since her brother's death, Makayla has come to believe that life is cruel and capricious, destroying everything that brings meaning and joy. Her faith in people and a higher power has been shaken, leaving her with an unshakeable sense of despair. She now sees the world as a dark and unpredictable place where anything can happen at any moment. Makayla's negative appraisals have seeped into every aspect of her life, influencing how she copes with her emotions. She often avoids going to work or studying, unable to muster the energy or motivation to focus on tasks that once brought her a sense of purpose. Staying up late has become a habit, as if delaying sleep might somehow put off the inevitable dawn and its painful memories. Her eating habits have also changed; she frequently restricts food intake, using undereating as a way to cope with the emptiness inside. These maladaptive strategies only seem to worsen her emotional state, however. By avoiding work and study, Makayla feels like she's losing herself in the process – further solidifying her negative appraisals about life being meaningless and destroyed by trauma. Her attempts to suppress memories through avoidance and distraction have failed; if anything, they've become more vivid and overwhelming. Makayla's occupation as a forensic analyst has also become a source of distress. She often finds herself working on cases involving sudden or traumatic deaths, which trigger her own painful memories and emotions. The daily exposure to these cases reinforces her negative appraisals about the world being a cruel place. As time goes by, Makayla feels like she's becoming trapped in this vicious cycle – one that seems impossible to break free from. She's starting to realize that her maladaptive strategies are only perpetuating her distress and reinforcing her negative appraisals. This realization has brought her to seek help, hoping to find a way out of the darkness and regain some semblance of control over her life. What Makayla fears most is losing herself completely in this abyss of grief and despair. She longs for a sense of meaning and purpose to return to her life, but it seems like an impossible dream right now. As she begins therapy, she's not sure if she'll be able to break free from the grip of trauma, but she knows she has to try – for herself, for her marriage, and for the memories of her beloved brother that continue to haunt her.
